title: Dashboard trust boundary: accept only known Host names and Origins (HTTP and WebSocket), limit login attempts, mark the cookie Secure outside loopback, add logout, and move money fields out of the public /health

options.name: Keep current behaviour
options.risk: A DNS-rebinding page passes CORS and can read /health and guess the key without limit (AUD-API-005); a same-site page can read the live feed over /ws (AUD-API-006); session cookies travel over plain http in remote mode and cannot be revoked (AUD-API-007); /health discloses positions and P&L and spends RPC calls for anyone (AUD-API-010).

options.name: Host allowlist and Origin check on HTTP and /ws, login backoff, Secure cookie whenever not loopback, logout and session revocation, money fields behind the session
options.behavior_impact: Requests with an unexpected Host or Origin are refused; remote setups must list their public name (DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS or a new host list); monitoring of /health keeps liveness only.
options.risk: A remote or proxied setup that is not listed stops working until configured; the vite dev proxy host must be in the list.

options.name: Refuse to bind anything but loopback; remote access only through an SSH tunnel or proxy that sets a fixed Host
options.risk: Removes a documented feature; rebinding (AUD-API-005) still needs the Host check because it works against loopback.

recommendation: harden-all, before the dashboard is ever exposed beyond 127.0.0.1; the Host check is needed even at loopback because rebinding targets loopback.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract); the items are S2/S3.
behavior_impact: Decides which browsers, pages and hosts can read or drive the dashboard API.
needed_by: Phase 29 discussion (S2-S4 fixes), or earlier if the dashboard will be reachable from anything but 127.0.0.1 before then
